html:
Aragon began as a small Christian kingdom in the central Pyrenees and grew into the Crown of Aragon, a sea power that ruled much of the western Mediterranean. On the map from 1000 to 1500 it grows from a mountain valley to a realm that, by 1492, includes Valencia, the Balearic Islands, Sardinia and Sicily.

It became a kingdom in 1035, when Sancho III of Navarre died and left it to his son Ramiro. Alfonso I, the Battler, took Zaragoza in 1118. In 1137 the heiress of Aragon was betrothed to the count of Barcelona, and the union joined Aragon to Catalonia and its port.

From then on the Crown looked to the sea:

  • James I, the Conqueror, took Majorca in 1229 and Valencia in 1238.
  • After the Sicilian Vespers of 1282, Peter III took Sicily.
  • Sardinia was invaded from 1323, and Sardinia became an Aragonese kingdom.
  • Alfonso V conquered Naples in 1442.

Barcelona's merchants traded across the Mediterranean under a shared code of sea law. Each of the realms kept its own laws and parliament, the Cortes, and the king had to bargain with them.

In 1469 Ferdinand II married Isabella of Castile, and their heirs ruled both crowns, the start of Spain. Aragon kept its own laws until the Nueva Planta decrees abolished them after the War of the Spanish Succession, between 1707 and 1716.
